concerns: The empirical base is a heavily skewed convenience sample: 88.9% of entries come from Google Research's self-selected public directory, and education data are missing for 89.8% of the 450 records, leaving only 46 senior, public-facing researchers for the substantive analysis.

The analysis is purely descriptive with no statistical models or causal identification, so claims about brain drain, environment-versus-training effects, and industry-wide mobility are not established beyond qualitative consistency with prior work.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The study provides basic descriptive tabulations on a heavily skewed convenience sample with nearly 90% missing educational data. Because the empirical base is small and non-representative, scientific confidence in broader conclusions is limited, justifying an uncertain rating.

evidence.excerpt:
The dataset has four major limitations. (1) Company imbalance: Google Research
is overrepresented (88.9% of entries) due to the accessibility of i ts public directory; the
label "MAANG" is therefore aspirational rather than descriptive of balanced coverage.
Future work should extend to Microsoft Research, OpenAI, NVIDIA Rese arch, Anthropic,
and IBM Research. (2) Education missingness: education data is absent for 89.8%
of researchers, restricting multivariate analyses to the focal sub set and raising concerns
about selection bias (biographical pages exist primarily for prominent re searchers). (3)
Citation proxy: citation counts are a noisy proxy for research impact and are field-inflate d
for NLP and computer vision relative to algorithm theory or hardware research . (4) No
statistical models: the analysis is descriptive. Adding regression models of the form
log(citations) ∼ PhD rank

blocking_reasons: The empirical base is a heavily skewed convenience sample: 88.9% of entries come from Google Research's self-selected public directory, and education data are missing for 89.8% of the 450 records, leaving only 46 senior, public-facing researchers for the substantive analysis.

The analysis is purely descriptive with no statistical models or causal identification, so claims about brain drain, environment-versus-training effects, and industry-wide mobility are not established beyond qualitative consistency with prior work.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No iterative model optimization, tuning, or learned evaluator is used in this descriptive bibliometric study.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Descriptive statistics computed directly over the curated focal subset using Google Scholar citation counts and institutional tallies.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Manual scraping, filtering, and curation criteria based on public directory presence and Google Scholar search labels.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: While broad claims regarding the 'brain drain' and the effects of environment versus training are framed carefully as qualitative patterns, the tiny and highly selected sample of 46 individuals cannot reliably substantiate conclusions about industry-wide research mobility or impact dynamics.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical evaluation is limited to elementary descriptive statistics (Gini coefficient, top-N shares, institutional frequency counts) on a highly non-random focal subset of 46 senior, public-facing researchers, with no formal statistical modeling or causal identification.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No iterative model optimization, tuning, or learned evaluator is utilized in this purely descriptive bibliometric study.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Descriptive statistics computed directly over the curated focal subset (Google Scholar citation counts and institutional tallies).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Manual scraping, filtering, and curation criteria based on public directory presence and Google Scholar search labels.

primary.limitations: The author transparently notes extreme company imbalance, substantial missing educational data, reliance on unadjusted Google Scholar citations, and the lack of inferential regression models.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology consists of opportunistic web scraping from Google Research directory pages and targeted Google Scholar label queries, leading to severe sampling bias (88.9% Google affiliates) and 89.8% missingness in education data across the 450 records.
primary.quality_rationale: The study provides basic descriptive tabulations on a heavily skewed convenience sample with nearly 90% missing educational data. Because the empirical base is small and non-representative, scientific confidence in broader conclusions is limited, justifying an uncertain rating.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript presents MAANG-AI-450, a descriptive dataset of 450 AI researchers across major technology companies, alongside a summary analysis of citation distributions and educational backgrounds for a focal subset of 46 researchers.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study provides basic descriptive tabulations on a heavily skewed convenience sample with nearly 90% missing educational data. Because the empirical base is small and non-representative, scientific confidence in broader conclusions is limited, justifying an uncertain rating.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The author transparently notes extreme company imbalance, substantial missing educational data, reliance on unadjusted Google Scholar citations, and the lack of inferential regression models.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
